limites_camera: Keeps the camera inside the level edges: it never shows the empty space beyond. All 0 = no limits.
a level 6480 pixels wide: minimum X 0, maximum X 6480, minimum Y 0, maximum Y 1080, with [[fixer_camera]] on the player.
electrocution: Lightning crackles around the object: it flashes in the lightning color, shakes and throws sparks. Duration 0 = endless (electric fence); intensity 0 = stop.
the wizard touches a trap: [[electrocution]] on the wizard (1 second), [[attendre]] 1 second, then [[recommencer_scene]].
NoeudEventStart: Runs only once, as soon as the scene starts.
place the enemies, show the starting score or start the music.
NoeudEventChaqueImage: Runs over and over, on every frame of the game (about 60 times per second).
follow the finger or check a condition all the time. Avoid putting [[jouer_musique]] or [[appeler_fonction]] under it.
NoeudEventFinClic: Runs when the player lifts their finger from the screen, anywhere.
stop shooting when the screen is released.
NoeudEventClicObjet: Runs when the finger touches the chosen object. With a tag ("# card") as the target, it fires for every object with that tag: the touched object becomes the involved object.
a « Jump » button, opening a chest, picking an answer.
NoeudEventFinClicObjet: Runs when the finger is lifted above the chosen object.
confirm a button only when it is released.
NoeudEventMaintenuObjet: Repeats on every frame as long as the finger stays on the chosen object.
left / right buttons: while you hold them, the character moves.
NoeudEventDoigtAppuye: Repeats on every frame as long as a finger is on the screen, anywhere.
make a ship climb while the screen is held (use doigt.x and doigt.y in formulas).
NoeudEventDebutGlisser: Runs when the player starts dragging the chosen object (it must be [[lang:insp_cb_deplacable]]).
enlarge a card when it is picked up.
NoeudEventFinGlisser: Runs when the player drops the object they were dragging.
check whether a puzzle piece is in the right place.
NoeudEventCollisionAB: Runs once, when object A starts touching object B. They must separate before it can run again. This is also the event to use for « entering a zone ».
the player touches the finish zone → next level.
NoeudEventSortieZone: Runs once, when object A stops touching object B (it leaves the zone).
close a door when the player walks away.
NoeudEventSurvolObjet: Runs when the finger, sliding across the screen, reaches the chosen object.
light up a button when the finger passes over it.
NoeudEventFinSurvol: Runs when the finger leaves the object it was over.
NoeudEventChoc: Runs when the chosen object (dynamic physics) lands on a floor or bounces.
play a landing sound or shake the camera.
NoeudEventVariableChange: Runs every time the value of the chosen variable changes.
when « vie » (health) changes, update the health bar.
NoeudEventPersonnalise: Your own event, with the name you choose. It is started by the [[appeler_evenement]] node in the same Blueprint.
a « GameOver » event called from several places.
NoeudEventBoutonAction: Runs when the player presses the scene's [[lang:obj_prefix_btnaction]] object (action button).
talk to a character or open a door in an adventure game.
NoeudEventCollisionTag: Runs once per contact when the chosen object touches an object with this tag. The touched object becomes the [[lang:noeud_objet_implique]]. The "Touched side" setting limits the event to one side of the object (top, bottom, left, right): "top of the object" means something comes down on it, for example an elevator crushing it. "Anywhere" (default) ignores the side.
the player touches a coin (tag « piece ») → destroy the involved object and add 1 to the score.
changer_scene: Leaves the current scene and goes to the chosen scene. This node ends the script.
go to the « Well done! » screen after the last level.
aller_scene_nom: Goes to the scene whose name you type (or a formula giving that name). This node ends the script.
a formula like ="Level" + level to choose the level with a variable.
scene_suivante: Goes to the scene placed just after in the scene list. This node ends the script.
the player reaches the finish → next level.
scene_precedente: Goes to the scene placed just before in the scene list. This node ends the script.
a « Back » button in a menu.
recommencer_scene: Restarts the scene from the beginning: objects back in place and local variables back to their starting value. Global variables do not change.
ouvrir_hud: Shows another scene on top of the game, like a layer (HUD), with its own Blueprint.
a pause menu or an inventory.
fermer_hud: the « Close » button of the pause menu.
placer_copie_scene: Places a copy of the chosen scene (prefab) in the game, at position X, Y.
spawn a group of enemies prepared in another scene.
detruire_copies_scene: Removes all copies of the chosen scene placed in the game.
clear all enemy groups at the end of a wave.
quitter_jeu: Closes the exported game. In the editor, nothing closes: use the stop button.
a « Quit » button in the main menu.
toast: Shows a small message at the bottom of the screen for a few seconds. Start with = to show a calculation.
journal: Writes a message in the project log (diagnostic file), without showing anything in the game. Start with = to write a calculation.
="health = " + vie, to check a value while testing.
fixer_camera: The camera follows the chosen object. You can make it follow only horizontally or vertically. With no object, the camera stops following.
follow the player through a big platform level.
elasticite_camera: Sets how fast the camera catches up with the followed object: 0.01 = very soft, 1 = stuck to the object.
0.1 for a smooth camera that follows with a slight delay.
tremblement_camera: Shakes the screen with the chosen strength and duration (in milliseconds).
vibration: Makes the phone vibrate for the chosen duration (in milliseconds). Without a vibration motor, nothing happens.
100 ms when the player gets hit.
sauvegarder_etat: Remembers the state of the scene (objects and variables) and the global variables, like a save point.
a checkpoint flag in the middle of the level.
restaurer_etat: Puts the scene back as it was at the last [[sauvegarder_etat]]. If there is no save yet, nothing changes.
start again from the checkpoint after a fall.
attendre: Waits for the chosen time, in seconds, then continues. The rest of the game keeps running during the wait.
show « You lose! », wait 2 seconds, then restart the scene.
repeter: Runs the [[lang:port_a_chaque_fois]] output every X seconds, a number of times (0 = forever), then [[lang:port_termine]]. [[lang:port_tout_de_suite]] runs at the start. If it is already running, it does not start again.
compte_a_rebours: Removes 1 from the chosen variable (a number) every second until 0. [[lang:port_chaque_seconde]] runs on each tick, [[lang:port_termine]] at 0. [[lang:compte_a_rebours.depart]] sets the starting value.
arreter_minuteur: Stops the timer (Repeat or Countdown) with this name, or all timers if the name is empty.
stop the timer when the player wins.
vitesse_jeu: Changes the speed of the whole game: 1 = normal, 0.5 = slow motion, 2 = fast (from 0 to 4).
pause_jeu: Pauses the game: movements and timers stop.
reprendre_jeu: Resumes the game after a pause.
the « Continue » button of the pause menu.
deplacer: Puts the object directly at position X, Y (teleport).
put the player back at the start.
pousser: Moves the object by the given distance from where it is now. A physics object is stopped by walls.
modifier_propriete: Changes an object property chosen from a list (x, y, rotation, opacity, text…).
set the rotation of a clock hand to =temps * 90.
rotation: Turns the object to the given angle, in degrees.
=wheel.rotation + 5 linked to [[NoeudEventChaqueImage]] keeps the object « wheel » spinning.
opacite: Sets the object's transparency: 0 = invisible, 1 = solid.
visibilite: show a « You win! » message hidden at the start.
definir_tag: Gives the object a new tag (label).
a defeated enemy gets the tag « harmless ».
changer_zorder: Changes the object's layer: the bigger the number, the more the object is in front of others.
put the player in front of a decoration.
modifier_taille: Changes the object's size: 1 = normal, 2 = twice as big, 0.5 = half.
the player grows after eating a mushroom.
detruire_objet: Removes the chosen object from the scene.
choose [[lang:noeud_objet_implique]] to destroy the coin the player just touched.
detruire_par_tag: Removes all objects with this tag.
a bomb destroys every « Enemy » object.
changer_image: Replaces the object's image with another image from the Assets. Empty = no image.
the character looks left or right depending on the button.
modifier_couleur: a button turns green when the answer is right.
generer_clone: Creates a copy of object B (the model) at the place of object A (the spawn point).
filtre_couleur: Applies a filter to the object: Black and White, Sepia, Invert, or None to remove it.
switch to black and white during a flashback.
mode_affichage: Changes how the object blends with what is behind it (Additive, Multiply, Screen, Invert).
Additive for a glowing light or flame.
miroir: Flips the object: Horizontal (left / right) or Vertical (up / down).
the character faces the way it walks.
modifier_verrouillage: Locks or unlocks the object in the editor (the padlock). It has no effect during the game: to stop an object from being dragged, use [[changer_comportement]].
parallaxe: Sets how fast the object scrolls when the camera moves: 1 = normal, 0.5 = half as fast (depth effect).
mountains in the background that scroll slowly.
lier_objets: Attaches object A (the child) to object B (the parent): A follows B when it moves.
a sword that follows the character's hand.
surbrillance: Surrounds the object with a soft glow of the chosen color and size (it follows the shape of images), or removes it.
a bonus that glows yellow, size 20.
clignotement: Makes the object blink at the chosen speed (ms), for a duration (ms, 0 = forever), or stops the blinking.
the player blinks for 1 second after being hit.
generer_clone_position: Creates a copy of object B (the model) at position X, Y. The copy becomes the [[lang:noeud_objet_implique]].
drop a rock at a random position: X = random(0, 800).
tirer: Creates a projectile (the object named in [[lang:tirer.modele]]) at object A, and launches it at the chosen speed: 0°, 90°, 180°, 270°, towards object B ([[lang:option.Vers la cible]]) or along A's angle.
modifier_progression: Sets how full a progress bar is, between its minimum and maximum.
traverser_ecran: Whatever leaves one side of the screen comes back on the opposite side (Pac-Man effect).
an asteroid that leaves on the right and comes back on the left.
garder_dans_ecran: Stops the object from leaving the screen. The margin stops it a little before the edge.
the player's ship always stays visible.
creer_objet: Creates a copy of the chosen object (the model) at position X, Y.
add a crate at an exact spot.
fondu: Smoothly changes the object's opacity to the target value, over the chosen time (seconds). The next nodes run without waiting.
fade out a title in 1 second (target opacity 0).
modifier_variable: Gives the variable a new value (a number, a text, yes / no or a calculation).
ajouter_variable: Adds the value to the variable (a negative number subtracts). For a text variable, adds the text at the end. With "Back to 0 after", the variable turns like a counter: after 9 it goes back to 0 (and below 0 it goes to 9).
score + 1 for each coin; a padlock digit: + 1 on each tap, back to 0 after 9.
limiter_valeur: Keeps the variable (a number) between a minimum and a maximum.
nombre_aleatoire: Puts a random number in the variable. random(1, 6) gives a number from 1 to 6.
ajouter_inventaire: Puts the object in the inventory (a variable of type Inventory List). It is only added once.
retirer_inventaire: Removes the object from the inventory.
use the key to open the door.
si_dans_inventaire: Follows the True output if the object is in the inventory, False otherwise.
the door only opens if the key is in the inventory.
combinaison: Replaces objects A and B with a copy of the object whose name you type, at A's place. If that model does not exist, nothing changes.
condition: Tests a condition: follows the True output if it is right, False otherwise. [[lang:port_ensuite]] runs afterwards, in both cases.
si_joystick: Follows the output matching the joystick direction: Up, Down, Left, Right, or Idle when it is not touched.
linked to [[NoeudEventChaqueImage]] to play the walking animation in the right direction.
si_au_sol: True if the bottom of the object is standing on a fixed, visible object (floor, platform), False otherwise.
only allow jumping when the player is on the ground.
si_en_mouvement: True if the object moved since the previous frame, False otherwise.
play the walking animation only when the character moves.
appeler_fonction: Runs a function (a Blueprint created in the Functions section), then continues. Do not put it under [[NoeudEventChaqueImage]].
a « LoseLife » function used by several enemies.
appeler_evenement: Runs the [[NoeudEventPersonnalise]] with this name, in the same Blueprint, then continues.
call « GameOver » from the fall and from the timer.
sequence: Runs its outputs one after the other: 1, then 2, then 3, then 4. An output with no link is skipped.
at start: 1 = place the player, 2 = start the music, 3 = show the score.
cooldown: Lets things through [[lang:port_pret]] at most once per delay (in seconds); otherwise it is [[lang:port_attente]]. With an object chosen, each object has its own delay.
shoot at most once every 0.5 second.
si_hors_ecran: True if the object is completely off the screen (plus the margin), False otherwise.
destroy bullets that leave the screen.
si_sinon: Tests the first condition, then the second: follows [[lang:port_si]], [[lang:port_sinon_si]] or [[lang:port_sinon]]. [[lang:port_ensuite]] runs afterwards.
if score >= 100 → gold, else if score >= 50 → silver, else → bronze.
selon_valeur: Compares the value to test with cases 1 to 6 and follows the output of the first matching case; [[lang:port_aucun]] if nothing matches. An empty case is skipped.
depending on « weapon »: 1 = sword, 2 = bow, 3 = wand.
modifier_texte: Replaces the text of a Text object. Start with = to show a calculation.
afficher_dialogue: Writes into the Text object the sentence matching the key, from the dialogue file (dialogues.txt). Several languages: write « hello.en = Hello », « hello.fr = Bonjour »…; the game uses the language in the « langue » variable, otherwise the phone language. « \n » = new line.
the key « hello_merchant » shows the merchant's line.
ajouter_au_texte: Adds text at the end of a variable of type Text.
type a password letter by letter.
arreter: Stops the object dead: no more speed, push, jump or automatic movement.
freeze an enemy hit by an ice spell.
stopper_mouvements: Turns off the object's automatic movements: move continuously, pursue and flee.
the enemy stops chasing when the player hides.
avancer_continu: The object moves by itself, in the direction it is facing, at the chosen speed.
a bullet or a moving car.
poursuivre: Object A moves by itself towards object B, at the chosen speed.
fuir: Object A moves by itself away from object B, at the chosen speed.
a chicken running away from the player.
changer_rebond: Sets how much a physics object bounces: 0 = no bounce, 1 = bounces a lot.
force_angle: Pushes the object in a direction (in degrees: 0 = right, 90 = down, 180 = left, 270 = up) with the chosen force.
a spring that sends the player diagonally.
impulsion: Launches the object upwards (negative number) or downwards (positive), and gives it physics so it falls back.
activer_physique: Gives the object physics: Falls = true, it falls with gravity; false, it stays fixed like a floor.
a platform that collapses when you walk on it.
modifier_deplacable: Allows (true) or forbids (false) dragging the object with the finger during the game.
lock a puzzle piece that is in the right place.
sautiller: Makes the object hop (a small visual bounce) with the chosen intensity and duration. 0 stops it. It can keep going while the object moves.
a character that hops as it walks.
orienter_vers: Turns object A towards object B. The offset fixes the image's direction (0 = the image faces right).
a turret aiming at the player.
glisser_vers: Smoothly moves the object to position X, Y over the chosen time (seconds). The next nodes run without waiting.
a moving platform or a menu sliding onto the screen.
jouer_animation: Plays one of the object's animations, at the chosen speed (frames per second), looping or once. If it is already playing, it continues without restarting.
the « walk » animation when the character moves.
arreter_animation: Stops the animation and goes back to its first frame.
pause_animation: Pauses the animation on the current frame.
freeze the character during a pause.
reprendre_animation: Resumes the animation where it was paused.
vitesse_animation: Changes the animation speed (frames per second) without restarting it.
jouer_son: Plays a sound effect. Several sounds can play at the same time.
a « bling » when a coin is picked up.
jouer_musique: Starts a music track, replacing the current one. Do not put it under [[NoeudEventChaqueImage]] (it would restart all the time).
arreter_musique: silence on the Game Over screen.
effet_particules: Fires a burst of particles on the object: explosion, sparks, dust, smoke, fire, rain, snow, confetti, trail, wake trail, hyperspace or speed lines. Count, color and size can be set. With an image ("Image" setting), each particle becomes that image: a drawn explosion, a star, a leaf…
a hit enemy explodes in magenta: Explosion preset, color #FF40D0.
particules_marche: Turns a “Particles” object on or off: it emits continuously or stops (particles already fired finish their life).
turn the engine exhaust on when the ship moves.
salve_particules: Fires many particles at once from a “Particles” object, with its settings (preset, color, size).
80 confetti when the level is won.
changer_modele_particules: Changes the preset of a “Particles” object during the game.
a fire that turns into smoke when it is put out.
flash_ecran: Flashes a color over the whole screen, fading out in a moment (intensity in %, duration in seconds).
a 0.5-second red flash when the player is hit.
teinte_ecran: Lays a color over the whole game (under the HUD), with a smooth transition. Intensity 0 removes it.
night falls: dark blue, intensity 55, 2-second transition.
bords_assombris: Gently darkens the edges of the screen, like in a movie (under the HUD). Intensity 0 removes it.
a scary mood in a cave: intensity 75.
fondu_ecran: Fades the whole screen out to a color, or back in from it. The fade carries over from one scene to the next.
[[fondu_ecran]] (fade out), [[attendre]] 1 second, [[changer_scene]], then [[fondu_ecran]] (fade in) when the next level starts.
trainee_objet: The object leaves a trail of particles behind it when it moves (preset, color and size of your choice). Set on a shot's model, every shot inherits it. Preset “None” removes it.
shots that leave a glowing trail: target = the shot's model, Trail preset.
arret_sur_image: Slows the whole game almost to a stop for a very short moment (in real seconds), then the game goes back to its speed. It gives “punch” to impacts.
when an enemy explodes: duration 0.06, speed 0.05.
chemin_vers_objet: Object A goes to object B, finding the shortest path by itself, square by square, without going through walls ("Solid" tiles of a tile layer, fixed physical objects). The path is updated when B moves. [[lang:port_arrive]] runs when A touches B. The "Stop" setting lets the object stop on a neighbouring cell, well centered (grid games); "These tags block the path" makes it go around other units.
a ghost chasing the player through a maze.
chemin_vers_point: Object A goes to point X, Y around the walls, by the shortest path (square by square). With =doigt.x and =doigt.y, it goes where the screen is touched. [[lang:port_arrive]] runs on arrival. If there is no path, it stays where it is.
tap a square to send the hero there, in a strategy game or a dungeon.
chemin_arreter: The object stops following its path ([[chemin_vers_objet]] or [[chemin_vers_point]]) and stays where it is.
the fly stops when the game is won.
grille_remplir: Splits object A (the board) into columns and rows and puts in each cell a copy of a model object picked at random (at least 3 models, names separated by commas). There is never a match at the start, and the pieces drop in from the top. Use it before [[grille_jouer]].
at the start, an 8 x 8 grid of candies "red, orange, yellow, green, blue, pink".
grille_jouer: The heart of a match-3 game (Candy Crush style), to put under [[NoeudEventDoigtAppuye]]. Touching a piece selects it, touching its neighbour (or sliding the finger to it) swaps them. The swap only stays if it lines up 3 or more identical pieces; otherwise they go back ([[lang:port_refuse]]). Each matched piece starts [[lang:port_aligne]] (the involved object is the piece), then disappears; pieces fall, new ones arrive and combos happen by themselves. When everything is still: [[lang:port_termine]]. With no possible move, the grid shuffles itself.
[[lang:port_aligne]]: +10 points and sparkles on the piece; [[lang:port_termine]]: one move less.
grille_melanger: Moves all the pieces of object A's grid to new places, without creating a match and keeping at least one possible move.
a "Shuffle" button when the player is stuck.
changer_comportement: Changes what the object does during the game, with the same choices as the Inspector's "Object behavior" window: Scenery, Ground / wall, Falls and bounces, Platform character, Patrol (back and forth), Top-down character, Dragged with a finger. You can also change the speed, the jump height, "is a ladder" and "collectable". Every setting left on "(don't change)" keeps its value.
a crate standing still (Ground / wall) starts to fall when a lever is pulled: Change the behavior → Falls and bounces.
melanger_places: Randomly swaps the places of all objects with the chosen tag (Object A = "# tag"). Their child objects follow them.
shuffle the cards of a memory game at the start, or the cups of a shell game.
valeur_hasard: Green node (value): gives a random number between "From" and "To", drawn again each time it is used. Connect it to a setting with the 🔗 button of the settings window.
make a coin appear at a random X between 0 and 800.
valeur_objet: Green node (value): gives a value of the chosen object during the game: its x or y position, width, rotation, opacity…
put a coin at the same height as the player (Y ← object value: player, y).
valeur_variable: Green node (value): gives the current value of a variable (score, lives…) during the game.
show the score in a text (Text ← variable value: score).
valeur_calcul: Green node (value): calculates A + B, A − B, A × B or A ÷ B. A and B can be numbers, or receive a green wire themselves (chained calculations).
give twice as many points (Value ← calculation: score × 2).
valeur_distance: Green node (value): gives the distance (in pixels) between the centers of two objects during the game.
shake the screen harder when the enemy is close.
dire_phrase: Dialogue game: the chosen character says the line in a dialogue box, letter by letter, and the player taps the screen to continue. The character appears with their emotion (their Character sheet: pictures, color, voice). Special words: [c]color[/c], [t]shake[/t], [o]wave[/o], [p] for a pause, {score} for a variable; "🌐 9 languages" button to translate.
Hana (happy) says "Hello!", then [[poser_choix]] offers two answers.
poser_choix: Shows 2 to 4 answers as big buttons: each answer goes out through its own output, so the story branches like a tree. An answer can require a condition (otherwise it is greyed out or hidden); an optional timer adds the "Time's up" output. Each answer can also have a picture (advanced settings): the answers become big illustrated cards.
"Open the treasure" leads to the good ending, "Leave" to the sad one.
changer_decor: Puts a picture as the background, full screen, behind the story's characters (fading or at once). Empty picture = no more background.
the meadow at the start, then the forest when Hana goes looking for her cat.
montrer_personnage: Brings a story character in (emotion, place, entrance: fade, slide, jump), changes their emotion or makes them leave, without speaking.
Lyn comes in from the right while Hana is talking.
terminer_histoire: Clears the dialogue box, the characters and the background of the story: the game takes over again. If you give an "Ending name", this ending is remembered forever and counts in "Endings and gallery" of the [[ecran_titre_histoire]]; the saved game is erased.
"Friends of the cabin" after the last line, then back to the title screen.
ecran_titre_histoire: Shows the story title over a picture, with big buttons: "Continue" (resumes where the player left off, with the background, characters, music and variables: the story saves itself at every line), "New game" (the output: the start of the story) and "Endings and gallery" (endings found and backgrounds already seen, the others are locked). During the story, the ◀ Back button returns to the previous line, even before a choice.
placed right after "At start"; every [[terminer_histoire]] comes back to it.
ambiance: Puts an atmosphere over the whole screen that stays until the next Atmosphere node: what falls or floats (rain, storm with lightning, snow, petals, leaves, fireflies, hearts, bubbles, mist) and a light (night, sunset, memory, dream, fear, dark). The old one fades out while the new one comes in.
after the "Leave" choice, storm and night light; "none" and "normal" remove everything.
zoom_ecran: Smoothly enlarges the whole game screen (the scene, or a story's background and characters) towards the center, the face, a side, the top or the bottom. 100 = back to normal; the dialogue box and the HUD don't move.
zoom 140 towards the face for 2 seconds when Hana is scared, then zoom 100.
transition_ecran: Covers or uncovers the screen with a shape (19 to choose from: circle, star, heart, curtain, clock, checkerboard, swirl…). “Close” covers the screen and it stays covered; “Open” uncovers it. “Next” runs when it's done, “Right away” runs immediately.
circle closing → [[changer_scene]] → circle opening. To change scene in a single step: [[changer_scene_transition]].
demander_texte: Opens a small window with the keyboard: the player types a text (their name…), stored in the chosen variable; it continues when they tap OK. In lines, {prenom} shows this text.
"What's your name?" → variable prenom → [[dire_phrase]] "Nice to meet you, {prenom}!".
changer_amitie: Adds (or removes, with −1) friendship hearts for a character, up to the maximum. The hearts show at the top left during the story and a “+1 ❤” floats up (they can be hidden in the Dialogue style). They are saved with the game and restored by ◀ Back.
after the kind answer “I'll stay with you”: Hana +1.
tester_amitie: Picks how the story goes on from a character's friendship hearts: the [[lang:port_vrai]] output if the comparison is true, otherwise [[lang:port_faux]]. For an ending that depends on how you treated the characters.
if Hana's friendship is at least 4 → the happy ending, otherwise the sad one.
filtre_ecran: Gives the whole game a “look”, buttons and texts included: TV, VHS, black and white, underwater, nightmare, flashlight… 32 filters to choose from. It fades in gently, stays as long as you want (0 = until you stop it) and can carry on into the next scene. “Then” runs right away, “When it's over” at the end of the duration.
the hero is hit: “Hurt” filter for 2 seconds; or “Flashlight” in a cave.
arreter_filtre: Gently fades out the current screen filter. “Then” runs right away, “When it's over” once the filter is gone.
the hero leaves the cave: stop the flashlight in 1 second.
changer_scene_transition: Changes scene with a transition: the screen is covered by a shape (circle, star, heart, curtain, swirl… 19 shapes), the new scene arrives, then the screen opens again. There is no output: what happens next is set in “At start” of the new scene.
the door is touched: go to the “House” scene with a circle closing on the hero.
NoeudEventBoutonRetour: Runs when the player presses the Back button of their phone (arrow or swipe gesture). Great for opening a pause menu or going back to the previous screen. Without this node, the Back button does nothing during the game.
Back → [[pause_jeu]], then show a “Resume / Quit” menu.
animer_personnage: Animates a character already on screen: it slides to another place, grows or shrinks, does little jumps or shakes. You set the duration and the style (even, smooth, quick then soft, slight overshoot, bounce). "Wait for the end" holds the story until the movement is over; otherwise the story goes on while it moves. The character must have been shown first with [[montrer_personnage]].
Hana slides from left to right with a bounce while she says "Wait for me!".
mode_roman: Switches to "novel mode": the text fills the whole screen over a darkened background and the lines of [[dire_phrase]] pile up one under the other, like in a book. When the page is full, it turns by itself. "New page" clears it right away; "Back to the dialogue box" brings back the usual box.
A night-time narration in novel mode, then back to the dialogue box for the conversation.
scene_rejouable: Marks a scene the player can watch again from "Endings and gallery" of the [[ecran_titre_histoire]] ("Scenes to replay" tab). Put one at the "Start of the scene": when the story passes it, the scene unlocks and the state of the story is remembered. Put another at the "End of the scene": when replaying, the story stops there and goes back to the gallery. Nothing is saved during a replay. Music started with [[jouer_musique]] also unlocks in the "Music" tab.
"The clearing": one node at the start of the meeting with Hana, another right after she leaves.
missile_guide: Launches a missile that starts in one direction, then slowly turns toward its target: it follows a real curve. “Object A” is the one that fires, “Object B” is the target to follow. The model is a hidden object whose image faces right. A small “Turn” gives a wide curve; when its lifetime ends, a missile that hit nothing explodes.
an enemy fires a missile at the ship: object A = the enemy, object B = the ship, lifetime 3 seconds.
detruire_apres: Removes the chosen object after a delay (in seconds). Handy to make an explosion disappear once its animation is over.
after [[generer_clone]] and [[jouer_animation]], the explosion image is destroyed 0.4 seconds later.
mode_sms: Shows the conversation as text messages on a phone: the lines of [[dire_phrase]] become bubbles (on the left for whoever writes, with three little dots "…" before they appear) and the answers of [[poser_choix]] are picked at the bottom of the phone, then arrive on the right. The narrator writes a small caption in the middle (for example "Last night, 10:14 pm"). "Who writes to you" gives the name and photo at the top; "Who is me" makes a character write on the right without going through a choice. "Clear the conversation" empties the phone; "Back to the dialogue box" leaves the mode. Everything is set in the Dialogue style: colours, size, time of the "…", full-screen phone…
SMS mode (turn on, who writes to you: Hana) → Say a line (Hana: "Are you there?") → Ask a choice ("Yes, tell me" / "Why?").
debloquer_succes: Unlocks an achievement: an "Achievement unlocked!" banner slides in at the top of the screen (only the first time in the published game; every time in the editor so you can see it). The achievement joins the "Achievements" tab of "Endings and gallery" of the [[ecran_titre_histoire]]: it stays hidden behind "???" (with a hint if you write one) until it is won. Put one at the end of a story, in a secret branch, after [[changer_amitie]]… The banner is set in the Dialogue style: colours, frame image, time, place (top or bottom), sound.
End the story (ending "The lost sock") → Unlock an achievement (name "The lost sock", description "Secret ending found").
jouer_mouvement: Plays on the object a movement made in Assets → Movement (steps: position, rotation, size, transparency). The engine computes everything in between. While it moves, the object's gravity and controls are switched off. The next nodes run without waiting.
a platform that goes up and down in a loop, or a sliding door.
arreter_mouvement: Stops the movement running on the object. It stays where it is.
stop the platform when the player presses a button.
passage_decor: Makes an image (bird, cloud, mosquito…) cross the background of a story, following a movement made in Assets → Movement. Choose behind or in front of the characters (the text box always stays on top). “Height” sets the size of the image. If the image is an animation (a bird flapping its wings), type its name in “Image animation” and the speed in “Speed (images per second)”.
a bird flying across the sky while Hana talks.
arreter_passages: Removes all the images currently crossing the story background (started by [[passage_decor]]).
the mosquito leaves when the dialogue is over.
sauvegarder_variables: Writes the values of your variables (global ones and the scene's) to a file on the device, so they are still there when the player closes and reopens the game. « Save name » lets you keep several games. Leave « Variables » empty to keep everything, or type names separated by commas (score, lives). Unlike [[sauvegarder_etat]], it survives closing the game.
When the player scores: [[ajouter_variable]] on « score », then [[sauvegarder_variables]]. The score is written to the file at every point.
charger_variables: Brings back the values written by [[sauvegarder_variables]] (same save name). Every variable that still exists gets its saved value back. Output « Loaded » when it worked, « No save found » on the very first game. Often placed right after « At start ».
Right after [[NoeudEventStart]]: [[charger_variables]], then [[modifier_propriete]] to show the score that was found.
placer_case: Puts object A exactly in the middle of the chosen cell (column and row, counted from 0 at the top left). The grid is the one of the scene's tile map. With the 🔗 button, plug in [[valeur_colonne_touchee]] and [[valeur_ligne_touchee]] to send it to the cell the finger touches.
move a piece to the touched cell in a board game.
centrer_case: Object A stays in its cell but goes back exactly to the middle. Handy when a move stopped between two cells.
re-center a hero after its move.
valeur_colonne_touchee: Green node (value): gives the column of the cell the finger touches (0 = the first on the left). Plug it into a setting with the 🔗 button.
know which column was touched to place a tower.
valeur_ligne_touchee: Green node (value): gives the row of the cell the finger touches (0 = the first at the top). Plug it into a setting with the 🔗 button.
know which row was touched to place a building.
valeur_colonne_objet: Green node (value): gives the column of the cell where the chosen object is (0 = the first on the left).
know in which column the hero is.
valeur_ligne_objet: Green node (value): gives the row of the cell where the chosen object is (0 = the first at the top).
know in which row the hero is.
tour_suivant: Passes the game to the next team. Write the teams in order using their tags (e.g. player,enemy). The first call (for example after "At start") begins with the first team; when every team has played, the turn number goes up. At the start of each turn the local event "tour_<team>" runs if it exists (e.g. "tour_enemy").
put "Go to the next turn" on the "End turn" button.
si_tour_de: True if it is the turn of the team written (its tag), False otherwise.
let the player touch their units only during their own turn.
marquer_joue: Remembers that the unit (object A) has played this turn. Everything is cleared when the next turn starts.
stop a hero from moving twice in the same turn.
si_a_joue: True if the unit (object A) has already played this turn, False otherwise.
refuse to move a hero that has already played.
valeur_numero_tour: Green node: the current turn number (1, 2, 3…), plug it in with the 🔗 button.
montrer_cases: Colors the cells the chosen object can move to (or attack). Walls block, and you can add tags that block (other units) and terrains that cost more steps (forest=2). Color, visibility, frame and numbers are adjustable. "Zone name" lets you show several at once (movement in blue, attack in red).
show a hero's movement zone when it is touched.
cacher_cases: Clears the colored cells (all of them, or one named zone).
hide the zone once the hero has arrived.
si_case_accessible: True if the cell (column, row) is one of the shown cells. By default: the cell the finger touches. False otherwise.
refuse a move that is too far with "too far!".
valeur_cout_case: Green node: the number of steps to reach the touched cell (-1 if it is outside the zone). Handy to count remaining steps.
remaining steps = the unit's steps - this number.
definir_vie: Gives health points to the chosen object (object variable "vie", and "vie_max" for the maximum). Read it anywhere with a formula, e.g. =monster.vie, to write it in a text or a bar.
give a monster 10 health points at the start.
infliger_degats: Removes health points from the object (never below 0). Two outputs: "Still alive" and "Out of health" (the object is destroyed if the box is ticked; "the involved object" stays the one hit).
a hero hits a monster: 3 damage, then a small message depending on the result.
soigner: Gives health points back to the object, without going over its maximum.
a potion that restores 5 health points to the hero.
valeur_terrain_touche: Green node: the name of the terrain of the touched cell ("Forest", "Water"…), or nothing if there is none. Terrains are set in the tile editor.
show "Forest" when a forest cell is touched.
valeur_cout_terrain_touche: Green node: the step cost of the terrain of the touched cell (1 if there is none).
say "this costs 2 steps" before a move.
valeur_terrain_objet: Green node: the name of the terrain the chosen object stands on.
know whether the hero is in water or on the road.
valeur_defense_objet: Green node: the defense bonus of the terrain under the chosen object.
chemin_vers_case: The object walks to the CENTER of the cell (column, row), going around walls, blocking terrains and the units with the given tags. Default: the cell touched by the finger. "Arrived" output once on the cell.
send a hero to a touched blue cell.
pion_une_case: Moves the piece one cell (up, down, left, right), well centered. If the cell is a wall, a blocking terrain, a unit (tags) or the edge of the map: "Blocked" output. Otherwise "Arrived" at the end of the step.
move a board-game piece with ◀ ▶ ▲ ▼ buttons.
definir_fiche: Gives the object its sheet: health, attack, defense, movement and range (object variables "vie", "attaque", "defense", "mouvement", "portee"). They can be read anywhere with a formula, e.g. =hero.mouvement for the number of steps of the reachable cells. Put this node "At start" of each unit, or in a reusable unit prefab.
create an archer: health 8, attack 4, defense 0, movement 4, range 3.
attaquer: Object A attacks object B: damage = A's attack × power − B's defense − B's terrain defense. Two exits: “Still alive” and “Out of health” (the target is destroyed if the box is ticked). Both objects need a unit sheet. In advanced: bonuses by tag (“cavalry = 150”: 150% damage against an object with the cavalry tag; an object can have several tags separated by commas), a free formula, and a statistic used up at each attack (“ammo”: at 0 the attack no longer happens).
A spear against cavalry: bonus “cavalry = 150”, so 150% damage; an archer using up “ammo”.
lumiere_ambiance: Darkens the whole game (under the buttons and score) with the color you choose. Darkness 0 = full daylight, 100 = pitch black, except around light sources. The level and the color change smoothly: over 30 seconds you go from day to an orange dusk and then a blue night, like a sunset.
a sunset: [[lumiere_ambiance]] orange, darkness 40, over 6 seconds; [[attendre]] 6 seconds; then [[lumiere_ambiance]] night blue, darkness 90, over 6 seconds.
lumiere_source: Attaches a light to the object: it follows the object when it moves (a character's torch, a lantern, a fire…), even if the object is the child of another. Settings: color, radius in pixels (distance from the center), lighting (100 = normal, up to 300: stronger and farther), colored glow (0 = none), flicker (none, candle, torch, flickers) and shift. One light per object, 8 at most at once. It cuts through the darkness set by [[lumiere_ambiance]]; without darkness it only adds its glow. « Switching on » setting: « Only when it is dark » turns the light on by itself at nightfall (ideal with [[lumiere_cycle]]).
a character's torch: placed on a « lantern » object that is a child of the hero, radius 360, flicker « torch ».
lumiere_eteindre: Turns off the light attached to the object. To turn it back on, use [[lumiere_source]] again.
a « Lantern » button turns off the hero's light.
ombre_objet: Puts a soft shadow under the object (or removes it with « No »). It follows the object when it moves; you can set its strength and width. It instantly gives volume to characters standing on a backdrop. You can also tick the « Shadow under the object » box in the Inspector, with no node at all.
a shadow under the hero: strength 50, width 70.
choisir_cible: Object A looks among the objects that carry one of the requested tags for those WITHIN ITS RANGE (same shapes as “Show reachable cells”), then picks one: the closest, the one with the least or the most health, or the lowest / highest value of a statistic. “Target found” output: it becomes “the involved object” (for Attack, Go to…). “No target” output: nobody in range. Perfect for the intelligence of a monster or a turret.
a monster: [[choisir_cible]] (tag “hero”, the closest, range =monster.range), then [[attaquer]] on “Target found”.
NoeudEventNouvelleScene: Runs every time a new scene opens. Made for the "Global logic" (which runs in every scene): for example, placing the chosen army on each map. In an ordinary scene, "On start" is enough.
lumiere_cycle: Takes the whole game from day to an orange evening, a blue night, dawn, then day again, all by itself. You choose the length of a full day (30 to 120 seconds for a lively game), the starting moment and whether the cycle repeats forever. A paused game freezes the cycle. Length 0 = stop the cycle (the sky stays as it is). A manual setting with [[lumiere_ambiance]] takes over. Your lights ([[lumiere_source]]) stay on: you see them better at night.
a living world: on start, [[lumiere_cycle]] with a length of 90 seconds, starting « Full day », looping.
physique_monde: Sets the physics world of the scene: gravity downwards (100% = normal, 0 = space, negative = objects fall upwards), sideways gravity (a wind that always blows), calculation precision and whether resting objects fall asleep. Use it once, under “At start”. It only affects objects that have the “Realistic physics” behavior (⚙ Behavior).
a level on the Moon: gravity 20%.
physique_changer: Changes the settings of a physics object during the game: its type (normal, fixed, guided, or no more physics), material (wood, stone, metal, rubber, ball, ice, feather), shape, weight, bounce, grip, gravity, air drag, top speed, whether it rotates, whether it is a ghost or very fast, its layer. Any setting left empty or on “(do not change)” stays as it is. On an object without physics yet, choosing a type gives it physics.
a ball that turns into rubber (material “Rubber”) when a bonus is picked up.
physique_pousser: Pushes a physics object with a force. “Steady push”: repeat it every frame (under “Every frame” or “Finger down”), the object speeds up as long as you push (a rocket, a wind, a fan). “A hit”: adds speed at once (a jump, a kick). By default the effect is the same on a light or heavy object; in the advanced settings you can make weight matter, and push away from the center to make the object spin. Values: pixels per second (per second squared for the steady push).
a rocket game: “Finger down” → push upwards (-2500) steadily.
physique_vitesse: Sets the speed of a physics object, in pixels per second: to the right, downwards (negative = upwards) and spin in degrees per second. Any box left empty leaves that speed unchanged. “Replace” gives exactly this speed; “Add” adds it to the current speed. The “Stop everything” option sets all speeds to zero. Perfect for a jump (downward speed of -900), a sharp stop or a character moving at constant speed.
a platformer jump: downward speed = -900, only if [[physique_test]] says the object is standing on something.
physique_lancer: Launches a physics object in a direction: you give the angle (0 = to the right, -90 = up, 90 = down, 180 = to the left) and the starting speed. Gravity then does the rest: the object follows a curve. Ideal for a slingshot game, a cannon, a ball throw. The angle can be a formula (for example the angle between the object and the finger).
a slingshot: when the finger lets go, launch the bird at the angle of the elastic.
physique_explosion: Blasts every physics object around a point: the closer to the center, the harder they are thrown, and they start to spin. The center is the middle of the chosen object, or an (x, y) point if you write one. You set the blast radius and the force (the speed given at the center). Option: only objects with a certain tag. The node destroys nothing: combine it with “Particle effect” and “Destroy object” for a real explosion.
a bomb: when it touches the ground, explosion with radius 500 and force 1800, then destroy the bomb.
physique_lier: Links two objects so they hold or move together, like in real life. Kind of link: hinge (swings around a point: door, pendulum), rigid rod (fixed distance), spring (elastic, with stiffness), rope (maximum length), slider (slides along a rail, with limits and motor), weld (stuck together), wheel with suspension (car: A = the body, B = the wheel, with motor), brake (top view). Object B is optional: without B, object A is attached to a fixed point of the scenery. Give the link a name to adjust it (“Adjust a link”) or cut it (“Cut a link”) later. In the advanced settings: point on each side, limits, rail direction, motor, collision between the two objects. Both objects need the “Realistic physics” behavior (except a fixed support).
a pendulum: A = the ball, B = a small fixed object at the top, type “Hinge” or “Rigid rod”; a bridge: planks linked by hinges.
physique_regler_liaison: Changes a link already created by “Link two objects” (found by its name): start, stop or speed up its motor, set its strength, the stiffness of a spring or suspension, the length of a rod or rope, the limits. Any empty box stays as before. Example: a car whose wheel motor starts when a button is pressed.
“Gas” button: adjust the link “rear_wheel” with motor = 720; on release: motor = 0.
physique_couper: Cuts a link: write its name, or write an object's name to cut all of its links. The objects separate and each falls on its own (a collapsing bridge, a cut rope, a detaching cabin).
a trapped bridge: when the hero touches the lever, cut the link “plank_3”.
physique_doigt: Lets you grab a physics object with the finger and drag it, like in real life: the object follows the finger with a bit of elasticity, pushes the others and can get stuck. Put it under “Finger down” (action “Grab and drag”): while the finger is down, the object under it is dragged; as soon as the finger lifts, it is released by itself (or use the “Let go” action). You can restrict the grab to objects with a tag, and set the softness of the grip.
a crate puzzle: the player moves crates with a fingertip to build a tower.
physique_test: Asks a question about a physics object and follows the “true” or “false” exit: is it standing on something (to allow a jump), does it touch something, does it touch something above, is it at rest (asleep), is it moving fast, falling, rising. For “moves fast”, “falling” and “rising” the threshold in pixels per second is set in the advanced settings. You can also read values directly in a formula: object.vitesse, object.masse, object.vitesseRotation.
a platformer jump: “Jump button” → If the object is standing on something → set downward speed to -900.
modifier_stat: Changes a statistic you invented for an object (ammo, armor, mana, fuel…): add to it, subtract from it or set it to a value. If it does not exist yet, it is created at 0. You can then read it anywhere: =archer.ammo.
After a shot: Change a statistic → object “archer”, statistic “ammo”, Subtract 1.
si_stat: Compares an object's statistic with a value and follows the “true” or “false” exit: for example “ammo is greater than 0”. A statistic that does not exist counts as 0.
Before shooting: If the archer's “ammo” statistic is greater than 0 → shoot; otherwise → show “Out of arrows”.
suivre_parcours: Makes the object follow a path drawn with the “Path” tool in Assets: it is placed on the starting point, then moves from point to point at the chosen speed. At a crossroads it picks its exit as you set it (random, take turns, by a variable). The “Reached the end” exit fires when it reaches a point with no exit. With “Random side offset”, each object walks in its own lane (random shift): several enemies advance side by side instead of overlapping. With “Avoid the others”, an object that catches up with a slower one steps aside, overtakes it and returns to its lane; if the road is too narrow, it follows instead.
An enemy appears: Follow the path “Enemy_path”, speed 150. “Reached the end” exit → Deal damage to the base, then Destroy the object.
arreter_parcours: Stops the object where it is: it no longer follows its path (the “Reached the end” exit will not fire).
An enemy is frozen by a trap: Stop the path, then later Follow the path again so it moves on.
camera_doigt: Turns finger scrolling on (or off): dragging in the scene moves the camera. A simple tap is still a tap (a tower, a button). HUD buttons never scroll. The camera stays inside the limits set with “Camera limits”.
On start: Camera limits (0, 3840, 0, 1080), then Scroll the camera with a finger: the player drags a map two screens wide.
